notes: HISTORICAL compatibility ceilings copied from the cited retired-harness run. cmd/eval enforces them fail-closed when -budgets is supplied — historical does not mean disabled — but they are NOT comparable post-change ratchets and must not be read as ones. Replace them only from a new current-harness run on the reference runner class declared in docs/eval/reference-scenario.json, against the re-frozen candidate; never rewrite historical reports. SW-123 (P0-A4) added the explicit historical/ratcheting declaration below and REMOVED the all-zero hero latency map that used to sit in this file. SW-191 (EVALBUDGET-001 closure) added the `historical_ceilings` block: comparison-class ceilings derived from the SW-191 two-dispatch campaign over guava, okio, kotlinx.serialization (SW-177 JVM matrix), flask, ky, and express. cmd/eval/budgets.go:97 now accepts a historical budget on the comparison class `local-sandbox`, which is the only class this block is read from. Each `notes` field carries the EVALFRESH-001 freshness block per repo.
historical_reason: The numbers come from run 29418826616 (commit 71353f9, 2026-07-15) under the previous harness, which measured a different workload: it omitted `impact` from the structural pool, required no semantic checks across all 12 Stable operations, used the earlier symbol sample, and sampled MAXRSS immediately after IngestAll instead of after the Stable-operation suite. A current measurement is therefore not comparable to these values, so they may bound a run but may never ratchet one. Re-baselining is blocked on SW-121 (re-frozen candidate) and SW-124 (comparable numbers on the reference class).
reference_scenario: docs/eval/reference-scenario.json — the runner class above must be the reference class declared there (asserted by cmd/eval/refscenario_test.go).

hero_suite.notes: SW-123 (P0-A4) REMOVED the `measured_max_latency_ms_per_op` map that used to sit here. It held 0 for all twelve Stable operations, because the historical run measured every hero task below the harness's millisecond-granularity floor on the tier-1 fixtures. Nothing read the map, and a zero budget that silently counts as met is worse than no budget: it renders green. The hero suite's gate is and remains the full scenario pass rate above; hero-task latency has NO budget, and `latency_signal: none` says so instead of a table of zeros implying one. cmd/eval now rejects any numeric zero anywhere in this artifact (cmd/eval/refscenario.go, validateNoSilentZeroBudgets). Per-operation latency gates live in docs/eval/reference-scenario.json against the reference scenario, not here against tier-1 fixtures.

real_repos.notes: These values came from the previous harness and are retained only as fail-closed upper compatibility limits. In those reports impact was absent from the structural pool and peak_rss_mb was sampled immediately after IngestAll; the 11821 MB guava value therefore cannot be attributed to agent_brief or Stable cache reads. The current harness includes impact, degree-stratified sampling, semantic checks, and stable_peak_rss_mb after all Stable operations. Until a new green ubuntu-latest matrix run is pinned, current comparable latency/RSS baselines and the cause of the historical guava peak are UNKNOWN.

historical_ceilings.notes: SW-191 (EVALBUDGET-001 closure). Comparison-class upper limits derived from the two-dispatch campaign over each pin; the worst per-dispatch value across both dispatches seeds `baseline`, and `budget` is a 2x-3x round-up to leave room for developer-machine variance and for the local-to-CI translation (the local-to-CI agent_brief ratio measured on Go pins is 0.61-0.81, so this block is NOT comparable post-change ratchets and must NOT be read as such — apply via the SW-191 historical branch in cmd/eval/budgets.go, never via the ratcheting one. EVALFRESH-001 freshness block per repo: the freshness/incremental suite is Go-only and aborts on every non-Go pin; this is documented per-repo below and is a known limitation, NOT a budget miss. The four perf suites listed per repo are cold_index, query_latency, incremental (Go-only) and progress_stalls; the python/ts/js pins publish three of four (incremental UNKNOWN, the others PASS).
